target_customer: Data engineering teams running Apache Spark workloads in AWS, GCP or Azure
problem: Spark is hard to configure, size and monitor, and managed offerings were costly. Data Mechanics ran Spark on Kubernetes inside the customer's own cloud account and automated tuning.
business_model: Managed platform, usage-based pricing on top of customer cloud
product_category: Data engineering platform, managed Spark on Kubernetes

founders.name: Jean-Yves Stephan
prior_employers: Databricks (about three years, Cloud Automation then tech lead of Cluster/Spark Infrastructure)
education: Ecole Polytechnique, undergraduate computer science and applied math
Stanford, master's in Management Science and Engineering
founders.background_notes: Source: Datacast interview write-up at jameskle.com. Worked as product manager at Spot after the acquisition per YC page.

founders.name: Julien Dumazert
founders.background_notes: Described as a long-time friend of Stephan and a Spark user; listed as founder on YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Autotuning Spark on Kubernetes, cluster sizing and an improved Spark UI required deep Spark infrastructure expertise, which the CEO had from Databricks.

defensibility.rationale: Open source Spark on Kubernetes was available to anyone and larger platforms could add similar autotuning.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: NetApp bought the company in June 2021 to speed up Spot Wave; the product continues as Ocean for Apache Spark.

market_need_then: Founders said they felt the pain of Databricks and competitors not solving cluster selection, sizing and Spark configuration far enough; early customers came from the CEO's Databricks relationships and content.

branding.domain_note: datamechanics.co was used; the domain now serves an unrelated gambling affiliate page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical, developer-oriented content marketing (blog posts, open source Delight Spark UI)

branding.brand_signature: Delight, the free open source Spark UI

rebrands.why: Folded into the Spot by NetApp product portfolio after acquisition

branding.community_and_virality: Open source Delight project and developer blog posts; no merch or fan evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic compound name; developer credibility came from content and Delight, no press about the brand itself found.

outcome_analysis: Two founders, one a former Databricks Spark infrastructure lead, built a managed Spark on Kubernetes platform during YC Summer 2019 and won early customers through content and the Delight open source tool. NetApp acquired the company in June 2021 for an undisclosed price to speed up its Spot Wave product, so the outcome was a strategic acquisition rather than an independent scale-up.
notes: Aggregators (Seedtable, StorageNewsletter) cite about $150K in 2019 from YC, Kima Ventures, Agoranov and Auren Hoffman; single aggregator figure, unverified, so not recorded as a round. The company website is now an unrelated casino affiliate page. A dated competitor search found no 2019 coverage naming rivals, so the list is empty, although Databricks was the incumbent the founders cite. Company name origin not found. Update: the seed round of about $150K (Seedtable dates it January 2019, CB Insights August 2019, so only the year is recorded) rests on a single database (Seedtable); CB Insights agrees on the $150K total. No press release found.
